content_json.original:
The growth of the use of English as the world’s primary language for international communication has obviously been continuing for several decades.
But even as the number of English speakers expands further there are signs that the global predominance of the language may fade within the foreseeable future.
Complex international, economic, technological and cultural changes could start to diminish the leading position of English as the language of the world market, and UK interests which enjoy advantage from the breadth of English usage would consequently face new pressures.
Those realistic possibilities are highlighted in the study presented by David Graddol.
His analysis should therefore end any self-contentedness among those who may believe that the global position of English is so stable that the young generations of the United Kingdom do not need additional language capabilities.
David Graddol concludes that monoglot English graduates face a bleak economic future as qualified multilingual youngsters from other countries are proving to have a competitive advantage over their British counterparts in global companies and organisations.
Alongside that, many countries are introducing English into the primary-school curriculum but British schoolchildren and students do not appear to be gaining greater encouragement to achieve fluency in other languages.
If left to themselves, such trends will diminish the relative strength of the English language in international education markets as the demand for educational resources in languages, such as Spanish, Arabic or Mandarin grows and international business process outsourcing in other language such as Japanese, French and German, spreads.
The changes identified by David Graddol all present clear and major challenges to the UK’s providers of English language teaching to people of other countries and to broader education business sectors.
The English language teaching sector directly earns nearly £1.3 billion for the UK in invisible exports and our other education related exports earn up to £10 billion a year more.
As the international education market expands, the recent slowdown in the number of international students studying in the main English-speaking countries is likely to continue, especially if there are no effective strategic policies to prevent such slippage.
The anticipation of possible shifts in demand provided by this study is significant: It gives a basis to all organisations which seek to promote the learning and use of English, a basis for planning to meet the possibilities of what could be a very different operating environment.
That is a necessary and practical approach.
In this as in much else, those who wish to influence the future must prepare for it.

content_json.reference_translation:
英语作为世界主要国际交流语言的使用增长显然已持续数十年。
但即便英语使用者数量进一步扩大,也有迹象表明该语言的全球主导地位可能在可预见的未来消退。
复杂的国际、经济、技术和文化变革可能开始削弱英语作为世界市场语言的领先地位,而因英语使用广泛而获益的英国利益方将因此面临新的压力。
大卫·格拉多尔提出的研究强调了这些现实可能性。
因此,他的分析应当终结那些认为英语全球地位稳固、英国年轻一代无需掌握其他语言能力者的自满情绪。
大卫·格拉多尔得出结论认为,单一英语毕业生面临黯淡的经济前景,因为来自其他国家具备资质的多语言年轻人正在全球性公司和组织中证明其相对于英国同行具有竞争优势。
与此同时,许多国家正将英语纳入小学课程,但英国学童和学生似乎并未获得更多鼓励以流利掌握其他语言。
若任其自然发展,随着对西班牙语、阿拉伯语或汉语普通话等语言教育资源的需求增长,以及日语、法语和德语等其他语言国际业务流程外包的扩展,这些趋势将削弱英语在国际教育市场中的相对实力。
大卫·格拉多尔指出的这些变化对英国面向他国的英语教学提供者及更广泛的教育产业部门均构成明确而重大的挑战。
英语教学行业通过无形出口直接为英国创收近13亿英镑,而其他教育相关出口每年还可再创收高达100亿英镑。
随着国际教育市场扩大,近期在主要英语国家学习的国际学生数量放缓的态势可能持续,尤其是在缺乏有效战略政策阻止这种下滑的情况下。
本研究对需求可能变化的预判意义重大:它为所有致力于推广英语学习和使用的组织提供了基础,以便规划应对可能截然不同的运营环境。
这是一种必要且务实的方法。
在这一点上如同在诸多其他方面,欲影响未来者必须为之预作准备。
